text.p: Stricken German consumer electronics maker Grundig AG on Wednesday rejected comments made by trade union leaders that the firm faced bankruptcy if it did not find a partner to replace Philips NV.
"Grundig won't go bankrupt, even if it does not find a new partner by this summer," a company spokesman told Reuters.

The spokesman was reacting to remarks made by Gerd Loboda, an official of the IG Metall trade union who sits on Grundig's works council, that the company faced bankruptcy by mid-year if it did not find a strategic partner.

Grundig's outgoing chief executive Pieter van der Wal, who had been due to work out notice of two months, quit with immediate effect on Tuesday. Van der Wal had demanded job cuts as part of a turnaround plan for the TV and stereo maker.
The company spokesman added that Grundig had liquid reserves of 100 million marks ($61 million) plus other assets like property and was in talks with banks on a medium-term financing plan.
Van der Wal had been appointed by Dutch electronics giant Philips, which at the turn of this year sought to dissolve a contract with the Max Grundig Foundation to manage Grundig.
Loboda said earlier that Grundig would know within a week if it could take legal action accusing Philips of ruining Grundig to promote its own lines of electronics.
"Everything that Philips does shows that Philips wants to have Grundig out of the market," Loboda said.
Last month Grundig, which lost an estimated 350 million marks last year, paid Philips 250 million marks in connection with the cancellation of the options.
The pact gave Philips control of Grundig even though it held only a 32 percent stake and options to buy the foundation's 68 percent holding.
